newsitem.title: USA: Interpore sees Q2 loss from acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Interpore sees Q2 loss from acquisition.

text.p: Interpore International Inc on Tuesday said it signed a definitive pact to sell its dental implant business to Steri-Oss Inc in a move that will generate a loss in the second quarter.

Interpore, a maker of synthetic bone graft materials, said Yorba Linda, Calif.-based Steri-Oss will make an initial cash payment of $1.5 million followed by a deferred cash payment of up to $1.5 million in January 1998.
Closing is set to take place on or before May 2, 1997.

Under the deal, the companies have negotiated a distribution agreement whereby Interpore will manufacture and provide its Interpore 200 bone void filler for worldwide distribution by Steri-Oss in the oral/maxillofacial market.
In addition, the company said it has named David Mercer as its chairman, replacing George Smyth Jr., who will remain as a board member. Smyth formerly headed Interpore's dental division.
